capitals.name: Bogotá (Santa Fe de Bogotá)
capitals.note: 'On January 12, 1815, Congress arrived in Santa Fe de Bogotá.' The royalists took Bogotá on 6 May 1816; the patriots had no seat in 1816-1819 and retook the city on 10 August 1819.

keyframe_review.note: 336,138 km2 fits the page: 'The Act was ratified by the provinces of Antioquia, Cartagena, Neiva, Pamplona and Tunja' (27 November 1811), and 'roughly corresponding to the territory of modern-day Colombia'. By the gazetteer the shape covers Antioquia, Bolívar, Boyacá, Santander, Córdoba, Casanare and Arauca but only a sliver of Cundinamarca, which 'had not accepted the Union', and almost nothing of Santa Marta (Magdalena), Popayán or Pasto, which the pages show outside. The page gives no area; Casanare and Arauca are not named on it (unverified).

335,600 km2, unchanged but for a few cells. The civil war between the federal provinces and the centralist Free State of Cundinamarca ran 'between 1812 and 1814' (this page). Chocó is not yet in the shape: the page's table has the 'Cundinamarca Province of Chocó (1811-1813)'.

380,792 km2 adds Chocó (174 cells by the gazetteer): the table has 'Province of Chocó (1813-1816)' among the federalists after the 'Cundinamarca Province of Chocó (1811-1813)'. Cundinamarca is still outside until 'December 1814' (United Provinces page), so the shape matches the year before the union.

correction.text: unchanged for 1815 and the first eight months of 1816; 1816-1819 are described by new-granada_1816

keyframe_review.note: 602,458 km2 adds Cundinamarca (forced into the Union in December 1814) and a wide stretch of the eastern plains (Meta and Vichada, 710 cells by the gazetteer) that no page opened names. It stands for 1815 and until the reconquest: Cartagena fell on 6 December 1815, Bogotá on 6 May 1816, and the infobox gives 'Reconquest by Spain: September 3, 1816'. From 1816 to 1819 only the Casanare plains stayed patriot (new-granada_1816); Cliopatria keeps the full shape to 1819.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1816-1819 (Cliopatria keeps the 1815 outline): after the reconquest the table lists the 'Exiled Army of New Granada (1816-1819)' and the 'Province of Casanare (1813-1819)'; Santander 'retreated to the eastern plains, near the border with Venezuela'. The Spanish reconquest page says the exiles 'resumed the struggle for independence in the remote border areas'. Casanare and Arauca are my reading of those plains; the pages give no boundary.

keyframe_review.note: 1,341,011 km2 for 1820-1821, with 191,000 km2 in modern Brazil and 6,500 km2 in Peru by the gazetteer, is not this state: it ended with 'The creation of Gran Colombia in December of 1819', and the shape is Colombia's claimed extent, not the land held. After Boyacá the battle 'led to the liberation of much of central New Granada' and 'fighting with royalist forces would continue for years' (the Viceroyalty dossier, am-06-x, has Cartagena and the Caribbean coast falling in 1821, Panama joining on 20 November 1821 and the viceroyalty ending at Pichincha on 24 May 1822). Use the Gran Colombia dossier for these years, with this core as the land held.

ledger.note: 27 November 1811: the Act of Federation. 'It issued an Act of Federation on November 27, 1811'; 'The Act was ratified by the provinces of Antioquia, Cartagena, Neiva, Pamplona and Tunja.' The infobox gives 'Independence declared: July 20, 1811' (the Colombian War of Independence page dates the Bogotá junta to 20 July 1810). The region is Cliopatria's 1811 shape, which is wider than the five named provinces.

region.text: the State of Cundinamarca around Bogotá

ledger.note: 1812: the federal provinces and Cundinamarca go to war. The Federalist First Republic of New Granada and the centralist Free and Independent State of Cundinamarca 'fought each other in a Civil war between 1812 and 1814'; Cundinamarca 'had not accepted the Union and, in fact, had even sent troops against it' (United Provinces page). The page gives no month or first battle.

1813: Chocó joins the federalists. The page's table moves the province from the 'Cundinamarca Province of Chocó (1811-1813)' to the 'Province of Chocó (1813-1816)' under the federalists; Cliopatria adds Chocó in 1814. The table gives years only.

region.text: the State of Cundinamarca around Bogotá

ledger.note: December 1814: Bolívar forces Cundinamarca into the Union. 'Bolívar's army had forced Cundinamarca into the Union in December 1814.'

region.text: the State of Cundinamarca around Bogotá

ledger.note: December 1814: Cundinamarca joins. The Congress's army 'headed by Simón Bolívar, had forced Cundinamarca into the Union in December 1814'; the Cliopatria shape of 1815 adds Cundinamarca (and the plains of Meta and Vichada, which the page does not mention).
12 January 1815: the Congress moves to Bogotá. 'On January 12, 1815, Congress arrived in Santa Fe de Bogotá' (the infobox capital is Tunja).

August 1815: Morillo's fleet reaches Cartagena. 'By mid August, Morillo and his forces set sail and arrived off Cartagena'; 'For the next five months, the Spanish laid a brutal siege that devastated the civilian population.'

region.text: the eastern cordillera from Cúcuta toward Bogotá

ledger.note: 18 October 1815: Calzada invades the interior. His V division 'began their invasion of New Granada' on 18 October 1815 from Guasdualito, crossing the Cordillera Oriental by the Chita Pass toward Cúcuta; he 'won the Battle of Cachirí in February 1816'.
6 December 1815: Cartagena falls. 'The fortified city finally fell on December 6, 1815.'
6 December 1815: Cartagena, the Caribbean port of the Union, goes to the royalists after the five-month siege.

region.text: the interior of New Granada around Bogotá: Cundinamarca and Boyacá

ledger.note: 6 May 1816: Bogotá falls. Calzada 'took the Republican capital Bogotá on 6 May 1816'; the republicans lost the Battle of Cuchilla del Tambo on 29 June 1816, and 'some 7,000 people were executed by the Spanish between 1816 and 1819'.

'The country was reconquered by Spain in 1816' (infobox 'Reconquest by Spain: September 3, 1816'); all the Union's land except the Casanare plains passes to the royalists. The exile community 'resumed the struggle for independence in the remote border areas' (Spanish reconquest page).

certainty.note: The Union was a federation of provinces whose frontiers the pages do not draw; the royalist enclaves (Santa Marta, Popayán, Pasto) are outside by name only. 1816-1819 is a guerrilla base.

notes:
WHAT THE ROW IS. Cliopatria's 'New Granada' (1811-1821) has the Wikipedia title of the viceroyalty but its shapes are the patriot side: 1811-1814 the federated provinces without Cundinamarca, 1815 with Cundinamarca, then the same outline to 1819 although Spain held it 1816-1819 (the Viceroyalty dossier's own 1816 'gain' counterpart is this state), and a 1.34 M km2 shape in 1820-1821 that is Colombia's claimed extent. The dossier is named for the United Provinces, which the page dates 1811-1816, and carries the Casanare rump (the Exiled Army of New Granada, 1816-1819) to the creation of Gran Colombia in December 1819. 'republic-of-new-granada' (1834-1858) is a different, later state.

NOT SETTLED. (1) The 1815 shape's Llanos (Meta, Vichada) and Caquetá are not named by any page opened; the Spanish reconquest page says nothing about which regions stayed patriot in 1816-1819, so the Casanare-and-Arauca rump rests on a table row and one sentence on Santander's retreat. (2) The pages do not date Cundinamarca's war start (only '1812') or give the Congress's seat before 1815 beyond the infobox 'Tunja'. (3) Provinces that never joined or joined late (Socorro, Mariquita, Popayán, Santa Marta, Panama, Pasto) are unresolved: the United Provinces page lists no membership beyond the five ratifiers. (4) The 1820-1821 shape is `wrong` here; the 'gran-colombia' dossier (another part) should start in December 1819 with the central New Granada core, or Cliopatria's 1820-1821 hole will be filled by nobody. (5) Panama, Magdalena and the Cauca stayed royalist until 1821-1822 (Viceroyalty dossier).

DISAGREEMENTS. The infobox says independence was declared 20 July 1811; the Colombian War of Independence page says the junta of Bogotá began the war on 20 July 1810 and declared independence on 26 July 1810. The infobox capital is Tunja while the text has the Congress arriving in Bogotá on 12 January 1815.

COUNTERPARTS. 'cundinamarca' (1814 row; another part), 'viceroyalty-of-new-granada' (am-06-x), 'gran-colombia' (another part). The Free States of Antioquia, Cartagena and Mariquita are named in the table as separate provinces of the federation and have no dossier; they are not needed as counterparts.

GAZETTEER. Every name resolved: 'New Granada (core)', Cartagena, the admin-1 units.
